content.thinking: No /usr/bin/time. Let me use Python timing instead.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/work && cat > runstress.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess, sys, time, resource
name = sys.argv[1]
data = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "stress.py", name], capture_output=True).stdout
t0 = time.monotonic()
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-B", "/workspace/submission/cli.py"],
                   input=data, capture_output=True)
t1 = time.monotonic()
ru = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
print(f"{name}: input {len(data)//1024}KiB, wall {t1-t0:.2f}s, "
      f"cpu {ru.ru_utime+ru.ru_stime:.2f}s, out {len(p.stdout)//1024}KiB, rc={p.returncode}")
EOF
for c in backlog restore_storm save_storm control cancel_inspect; do python3 runstress.py $c; done
